items.title: Russian Defence Ministry says overnight strikes hit military-linked facilities across Ukraine
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its overnight missile-and-drone attack struck defence-industry enterprises, storage terminals, energy sites and transport infrastructure in Kyiv and five Ukrainian regions, including Lviv and Ivano-Frankivsk. The ministry described the targets as connected to Ukraine's armed forces; its statement did not establish the extent of damage.

items.title: Reports describe emergency power cuts in Lviv and outages in Kryvyi Rih
items.summary: Emergency electricity outages were reported in Lviv and power losses in Kryvyi Rih following the overnight strikes. Trolleybus services were also reportedly suspended in several Kyiv districts, adding to disruption after the attacks.

items.title: Russia says air defences intercepted 310 Ukrainian drones overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry reported that its air defences shot down 310 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions during the night. The statement did not provide a regional breakdown or independently assessed damage figures.

items.title: Luhansk authorities report three killed in Ukrainian drone attack on residential buildings
items.summary: Russian-installed Luhansk leader Leonid Pasechnik said a Ukrainian drone attack struck apartment buildings in Yuvileine near Luhansk, killing three people and injuring six, including a child. Concrete floors reportedly collapsed in one building, and rescuers were searching for people who might remain trapped.

items.title: Russian deputy foreign minister rejects even quasi-NATO membership for Ukraine
items.summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said that even a form of quasi-membership for Ukraine in NATO would be unacceptable to Moscow. His statement underscores Russia's opposition to security arrangements resembling alliance membership.

items.title: Russia says no agreement reached on next round of Ukraine negotiations
items.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said there is no agreement on holding another round of negotiations over Ukraine. He gave the statement in response to a question about the next stage of talks.

items.title: NABU and SAPO announce bribery suspicions involving former SBU official
items.summary: NABU and SAPO say a former Ukrainian Security Service unit chief is suspected of leaking confidential investigative information in exchange for benefits, including a BMW X5 and a family hotel stay valued at 160,000 hryvnias. A business associate linked to the Privat group and a former Ukrgasvydobuvannya executive also received notices of suspicion; the investigation remains ongoing.

items.title: Poland investigates possible airspace violations during Russian attack on Ukraine
items.summary: Polish military authorities are reportedly investigating two possible airspace violations during the overnight Russian strikes on Ukraine. An unidentified flying object was found near Lipowiec in eastern Poland after radar indications of a possible fall in Bilgoraj County; Rzeszow airport temporarily suspended operations.

items.title: Report alleges three Kyiv water utility workers killed during missile strikes
items.summary: A Russian military-linked account says three Kyivvodokanal employees were killed and about 15 people injured when critical infrastructure was hit during the overnight strikes on Kyiv. The same account reports fires at an office building and other sites; the casualty figures are attributed to that report.

items.title: Russia identifies alleged missile-production and transport targets in overnight attack
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its overnight strikes hit a Fire Point missile assembly facility near Kyiv, an aircraft plant in Lviv allegedly producing Flamingo missiles, and the Zatoka road-rail bridge in Odesa region. These specific target claims expand on its earlier general account of the attack; the ministry did not provide an independently established damage assessment.

items.title: Ukraine says nuclear plants reduced output after strikes on power grid
items.summary: Ukraine's Energy Ministry said nuclear power plants were forced to reduce electricity generation after overnight strikes damaged power stations, substations and transmission infrastructure. The plants themselves were not reported to have been directly hit.

items.title: DTEK reports over 41,000 customers without power in Odesa region
items.summary: Ukrainian energy company DTEK reported that an attack on one of its facilities in Odesa region left more than 41,000 customers without electricity. The outage adds to disruption from the wider overnight strikes.

items.title: Medvedev rejects proposal to trade Ukrainian territory for NATO membership
items.summary: Former Russian president Dmitry Medvedev dismissed the idea of Ukraine joining a revised NATO in exchange for territorial concessions as absurd. He reiterated Moscow's opposition to Ukraine entering the alliance and suggested that such a trade would be unacceptable.

items.title: Russia says it will raise Luhansk residential drone strike with UN and OSCE
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry plans to immediately submit materials concerning the reported Ukrainian drone strike on residential buildings in Yuvileine, Luhansk, to Russian representatives at the United Nations and OSCE, according to official Rodion Miroshnik. Local authorities earlier reported three deaths and six injuries.

items.title: SAPO reports bail set in alleged Transnistria draft-evasion smuggling case
items.summary: SAPO says Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court set bail at 500,000 hryvnias for a suspect investigators consider the organizer of a scheme to smuggle military-age men through Transnistria into Europe. The court also imposed travel and reporting restrictions; investigators have completed the pretrial investigation and opened case materials to the defence.

items.title: Ryabkov says European visit to Moscow would not join Ukraine talks format
items.summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Moscow could promptly arrange a visit by representatives of three European countries if they accept its invitation. He stressed that the invitation does not mean European representatives would join the existing Russia-US-Ukraine negotiating format.

items.title: Smolensk governor reports damage to energy site and home after Ukrainian attack
items.summary: Smolensk regional governor Vasily Anokhin said an overnight large-scale Ukrainian attack damaged an energy facility, a civilian industrial site and a private residence in the Russian region. His statement did not specify casualties or the extent of the damage.

items.title: Kyiv water supply disrupted after strikes damage utility infrastructure
items.summary: Local utility services reportedly said Kyivvodokanal facilities were damaged and attacks on the power system disrupted water supplies in the capital. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged residents to work remotely where possible because of damaged bridges, while emergency power cuts were also reported in Dnipropetrovsk region.

items.title: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell on its territory
items.summary: Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone fell in Poland during the overnight attack on Ukraine. He identified debris from a Kh-101 missile near Nowy Lipowiec, another missile near Rudnik nad Sanem and a drone near Molodycz; no casualties or damage were reported.

items.title: Russia claims 6,808 Ukrainian drones intercepted over the past week
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted 6,808 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones, 13 Flamingo missiles and eight Neptune missiles over the past week. It also claimed two large-scale and 11 group strikes against Ukrainian military-industrial, energy and airfield targets, without providing independently established damage figures.

items.title: Water supply halted in Vyshneve amid Kyiv sewer restrictions
items.summary: The local water utility reportedly halted water supply in Vyshneve, Kyiv region, after Kyiv's sewer network restricted wastewater intake following the overnight attack. The disruption adds to water and power service problems reported around the capital.

items.title: Estonia reportedly plans to close all road border crossings with Russia on December 1
items.summary: Estonia's government reportedly decided to close all road border checkpoints with Russia from December 1. Latvia's border guard chief warned the move could redirect traffic toward Latvian crossings and increase staffing demands.

items.title: Moldovan parliament advances military-technical cooperation agreement with Ukraine
items.summary: Moldova's parliament reportedly approved a first reading of an agreement with Ukraine covering military equipment maintenance, cyber defence, critical infrastructure protection, training and non-lethal equipment. The proposal is not yet final legislation.

items.title: Tusk says US allies want to avoid escalation after missiles and drone fell in Poland
items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incidents in Polish airspace require a response but that allies including the United States are reluctant to risk a further escalation. He said he does not always agree with Washington's assessment of such incidents.

items.title: Putin calls on Ukrainians to seek closer ties with Russia
items.summary: In remarks aired on Russian television, President Vladimir Putin urged Ukrainians to consider their children's future and move toward closer ties with Russia. He accused Ukraine's nationalist leadership and Western supporters of acting against Ukrainians' interests.

items.title: Russian military commentary says Kyiv bridges remain usable after strikes
items.summary: A Russian military-linked assessment said traffic had largely resumed across Kyiv's bridges after the overnight attack, although some crossings still faced restrictions. The account acknowledged that the strikes had not caused bridge collapses or critical structural damage.

items.title: Britain and Norway reportedly plan two missile-armed patrol boats for Ukraine
items.summary: Britain and Norway reportedly plan to share more than £100 million in costs to build two 30-metre fast combat boats for Ukraine's navy at British shipyards. The vessels are expected to carry missiles and air-defence systems under the countries' maritime support initiative, although construction and delivery dates were not specified.

items.title: Russia claims daytime strikes on Ukrainian logistics, energy and port facilities
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said drone strikes hit a military-linked logistics centre in Horodnia, Chernihiv region, the Slobozhanska thermal power facility in Kharkiv region, and a cargo ship and port infrastructure in Chornomorsk, Odesa region. It also claimed a locomotive used for military supplies was struck near Riadove in Dnipropetrovsk region.

items.title: Report describes Russia's new Kub-10ME long-range attack drone
items.summary: Russian forces have reportedly begun using the Kub-10ME loitering munition, described as having a range exceeding 100 kilometres and optoelectronic guidance for moving targets. Its manufacturer claims day-and-night operation and improved resistance to electronic warfare; the reported specifications do not establish its battlefield effectiveness.

items.title: Russia summons Romanian ambassador over visas denied to young taekwondo athletes
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry said it summoned Romania's ambassador on November 20 to protest the refusal of entry visas to its youth taekwondo team for European championships in Bucharest. Moscow called the decision nationality-based discrimination and warned of consequences, amid wider restrictions affecting Russian participation in international sport.

items.title: Russia summons Estonian diplomat over planned border closure
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry summoned Estonia's acting chargé d'affaires to protest Tallinn's decision to close border checkpoints. Moscow called the move confrontational and warned that attempts to isolate Russia would carry serious economic and social consequences for Estonia.

items.title: Russia responds after Austria alleges damage to its Kyiv diplomatic mission
items.summary: Russia's embassy said it had repeatedly warned foreign diplomats, including Austrians, about the dangers of remaining in Ukraine and placed responsibility for potential consequences on Vienna. Austrian leaders had earlier accused Russia of striking their diplomatic mission's building in Kyiv.

items.title: Russian military claims drone strikes on Ukrainian supply vehicles in Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said drones operated by Novorossiysk airborne troops struck ground robotic supply vehicles carrying fuel, ammunition and food, as well as infantry pickup trucks, in Zaporizhzhia region. The ministry did not specify the number of vehicles destroyed.

items.title: Trump administration reportedly seeks Ukraine peace agreement by early January
items.summary: The Trump administration has reportedly told Ukrainian and European officials it wants a Russia-Ukraine peace agreement by early January, with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner pressing for faster negotiations. Kyiv is concerned that a rushed deal could involve territorial concessions, while Moscow is reportedly reluctant to agree without its key demands being met.

items.title: Poland puts Patriot air defences on alert after reported missile and drone incursions
items.summary: Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz reportedly ordered Patriot batteries near Rzeszow-Jasionka and Swidnik onto combat alert after debris from two missiles and a suspected drone was found in Poland. Additional air-defence systems, helicopters and territorial units were mobilized following the reported airspace violations.

items.title: Britain says multinational force for Ukraine is ready once fighting ends
items.summary: Britain's defence secretary said the coalition of willing countries remains committed to deploying personnel to Ukraine despite Russian objections. Speaking during multinational exercises, he said the force is prepared to begin its tasks once hostilities cease.

items.title: Report says Ukrainian grain transit through Romania's Constanta port has surged
items.summary: A report citing port operator data says 1.65 million tonnes of Ukrainian products passed through Romania's Constanta port from January to October 2026, five times the volume a year earlier but far below the 11.7 million tonnes recorded in the same period of 2023. The shift comes amid disruption to Ukraine's Black Sea export routes from Russian strikes.

items.title: EU-sanctioned Irish journalist alleges banking restrictions are affecting his family
items.summary: Irish journalist Chay Bowes says EU sanctions related to his Russia-Ukraine commentary have led to the closure of his and his wife's bank accounts and blocked access to payment services. He says his family must seek a licence from Ireland's central bank to access money for basic expenses; the allegations concern the personal impact of the sanctions.

items.title: Denmark expels Russian military attache, giving diplomat seven days to leave
items.summary: Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said Copenhagen has declared Russia's military attache persona non grata and ordered the diplomat to leave within seven days. He said the decision was communicated to Russia's ambassador during a meeting at the Danish Foreign Ministry.

items.title: Russian military-linked report alleges drone strike on Ukrainian unit in Chuhuiv
items.summary: A Russian military-linked account posted what it described as the aftermath of a jet-powered drone strike on an administrative building in Chuhuiv, Kharkiv region, allegedly used by a Ukrainian drone unit. The report provided a location but no casualty or damage figures.

items.title: Trump says Ukraine peace talks are progressing but defers security guarantees
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said Washington sees good prospects for a negotiated settlement and described Vladimir Putin as interested in peace. He said he was not ready to discuss potential security guarantees for Ukraine before an agreement is reached.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly receives nearly €8 billion in EU budget support
items.summary: Ukraine reportedly received nearly €8 billion in European Union budget assistance, described as the largest single disbursement under the programme. The funding comes as Kyiv continues to depend on international financial support during the war.

items.title: German-backed venture plans production of Ukrainian-designed FPV drones
items.summary: US technology company Auterion and Ukrainian manufacturer SkyFall reportedly agreed to establish a joint venture in Germany to produce Shrike attack drones. The German government is said to be considering hundreds of millions of euros in funding for production and procurement.

items.title: Reports describe missile impact and fire in Kryvyi Rih
items.summary: A Russian ballistic missile reportedly struck a building in Kryvyi Rih, with nearby restaurant windows blown out by the blast. Separate accounts reported a fire in the city and additional strikes in Kharkiv, without providing casualty figures.

items.title: Kyiv district official discusses temporary pit toilets amid infrastructure disruptions
items.summary: Desnianskyi district administrator Maksym Bakhmatov discussed using temporary pit-style toilets as continued strikes threaten Kyiv's sanitation infrastructure. He said facilities could be installed in enclosed structures and referred to the needs of roughly 300,000 residents in the district.

items.title: Kryvyi Rih water pressure falls after reported missile strikes disable pumping station
items.summary: A local water utility reportedly said missile strikes stopped a pumping station in Kryvyi Rih, leaving three city districts with reduced water pressure or temporary supply outages. The disruption follows earlier reports of missile impacts and fires in the city.

items.title: Sevastopol governor outlines alternative passenger routes after Crimean Bridge attack
items.summary: Governor Mikhail Razvozhaev said reserve supply routes are keeping food, medicine and fuel deliveries to Sevastopol operating despite the attack on the Crimean Bridge. He said passenger travel is the main challenge, with bus-to-rail transfers being arranged in Kerch and possible sea services under consideration.

items.title: Russian court freezes 57 million rubles in defence procurement corruption case
items.summary: Russia's Investigative Committee said a Rostov court seized property, cash and bank accounts worth 57 million rubles belonging to three defendants, including former Zvezda-Strela director Alexander Shafranovich. Investigators allege the group inflated prices for defence-related products, misappropriating more than 110 million rubles, and engaged in bribery; the allegations remain before the courts.

items.title: Russian marines reportedly intercept Ukrainian DARTS attack drone
items.summary: A Russian military-linked report says an interceptor drone called Yolka, operated by Russia's 40th Marine Brigade, struck a Ukrainian DARTS fixed-wing attack drone as it descended toward a target. The account describes an interception but does not identify the location or report further damage.

items.title: Ukrainian lawmaker says Russia is testing Geran-6 high-speed cruise missile
items.summary: Ukrainian parliamentary defence committee member Fedir Venislavskyi reportedly said Russia is testing a compact cruise missile designated Geran-6, expected to reach speeds of up to 1,000 km/h. The statement describes a system under testing rather than confirmed operational deployment.

items.title: Sweden summons Russian ambassador over explosion near its Kyiv embassy
items.summary: Sweden's Foreign Ministry summoned Russia's ambassador to protest an explosion near the Swedish embassy during Russian strikes on Kyiv on November 19, according to the Russian diplomatic mission. The diplomatic protest follows reports of damage or nearby impacts at other foreign missions in Kyiv.

items.title: Jeffrey Sachs urges US to rule out NATO membership for Ukraine and Georgia
items.summary: Economist Jeffrey Sachs said Washington should take the decisive step in dialogue with Moscow by publicly ruling out a US military alliance with Ukraine or Georgia and opposition to their NATO accession. He made the proposal after speaking with Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen; it is his recommendation, not an announced US policy.

items.title: Report alleges Ukrainian authorities forcibly mobilized Orthodox cleric
items.summary: A report alleges that Hierodeacon David Rusynchak of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church's Rivne diocese was detained in Odesa and transferred to a training centre in Zhytomyr. It claims his relatives have lost contact with him and that deployment to the Donetsk front is planned for December 5; these details are presented as allegations, not established findings.

items.title: Russian aircraft manufacturer reports new delivery of Su-57 fighters to Defence Ministry
items.summary: Russia's United Aircraft Corporation reportedly delivered another batch of Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jets to the Defence Ministry. The announcement did not specify how many aircraft were delivered; accompanying commentary promoted their capabilities and claimed they have operated against targets in Ukraine.

items.title: Report says Zakarpattia recruiters promise post-contract deferment to young volunteers
items.summary: A Russian military-linked report says Ukrainian recruitment officials in Zakarpattia are advertising a deferment from further mobilization after completion of a one-year contract under the 18–24 volunteer programme. The report criticizes the risks faced by recruits but provides no evidence of specific casualties tied to the offer.

items.title: Pistorius urges Europeans to consider Putin's invitation for Ukraine talks
items.summary: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius urged European leaders not to dismiss Vladimir Putin's invitation to visit Moscow for talks on Ukraine. He said initial signals of willingness to engage should be taken seriously, according to a report quoting his remarks.

items.title: Major fire destroys much of Kyiv shopping complex housing delivery and bank branches
items.summary: A large fire reportedly swept through a shopping complex in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, damaging premises used by ECO Market, delivery firm Nova Poshta and PrivatBank. The report said the blaze spread rapidly but did not establish its cause or link it to a military strike.

items.title: Russian envoy mocks German defence minister over dispute on strikes inside Russia
items.summary: Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev mocked German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius after a dispute involving US defence official Elbridge Colby. Colby had argued that Ukrainian long-range strikes inside Russia strengthen Russian public resolve rather than end the war, while Pistorius called criticism of the strikes foolish; Dmitriev responded sarcastically to an apology reportedly made by Pistorius.

items.title: Russian court upholds in-absentia arrest orders for American and Norwegian fighters
items.summary: A Russian court upheld in-absentia arrest orders for US and Norwegian nationals identified as Foster and Vinje over their alleged participation in combat alongside Ukrainian forces, according to court documents cited in Russian reporting. Both have reportedly been placed on an international wanted list.

items.title: Zelensky says Ukraine will get through winter 'with great difficulty'
items.summary: Asked by CNN how Ukraine plans to survive the coming winter, President Volodymyr Zelensky replied, 'With great difficulty.' His remarks come amid concerns over damage to energy infrastructure and the effects of continued fighting on major Ukrainian cities.

items.title: Russian court's in-absentia arrest order for former Ukrainian defence minister takes effect
items.summary: Russian court documents reportedly show that an in-absentia arrest order against former Ukrainian defence minister Oleksii Reznikov has entered into force. Russian authorities accuse him of particularly serious crimes against civilians in Donbas; the order reflects Russian legal proceedings, not a conviction.

items.title: Zelensky declines to explain why Trump reportedly blames him for the war
items.summary: Asked why US President Donald Trump continues to blame him for the war and says he should consider stepping down, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky replied that he thinks he knows the reason but is unsure whether he should discuss it openly. He did not elaborate in the quoted exchange.
